logline: A wealthy Mexico City family's floral empire and its secret cabaret double life collapse simultaneously when the patriarch's mistress shows up - exposing lies, affairs, and decades of upper-class dysfunction.

bollymeter.basis: 83% on Rotten Tomatoes (6 critics). Critics praised its dark-comedy timing, Verónica Castro's performance, and its subversion of the telenovela form.

pull_quotes.text: The House Of Flowers is a classic telenovela, and a good one.
Couple these modern updates with the addictive quality of a classic soap for a fun, not-so-guilty pleasure.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of La Casa de las Flores landed on Netflix in August 2018 and quickly became one of Netflix Mexico's most-discussed originals. Critics noted that creator Manolo Caro was doing something structurally unusual: wrapping queer storylines, class satire, and pitch-black comedy inside the scaffolding of a telenovela. Verónica Castro as matriarch Virginia de la Mora became a cultural talking point. The Decider review called it a classic telenovela done well; Refinery29 compared the family dysfunction to Succession. With 83% on Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics, Season 1 established the show as a prestige Latin American comedy in the same vein as Netflix's best international acquisitions.

episode_reviews.title: La Monarca
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere engineers a spectacular family crisis in its first act - establishing the de la Mora family's architectural hypocrisy with remarkable economy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The cabaret reveal that splits the family's public face from its actual income source.

seasons.review_body: Season 2, released in October 2019, maintained the show's dark-comic sensibility while pushing several characters further into their most dysfunctional arcs. The season's 9-episode run felt tighter than Season 1, and the LGBTQ storylines - including Julián's relationship and Elena's sexuality - received wider critical attention internationally. No aggregated critic score appeared on Rotten Tomatoes, but audience engagement on Netflix remained strong based on reported international viewership trends. The season deepened the family mythology without losing the camp pleasure that made Season 1 compulsive viewing.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 compresses the storytelling and leans harder into the queer narratives that distinguished the show from conventional telenovela fare.

seasons.review_body: The final season dropped in April 2020 during the global lockdown period, which shaped its reception - Netflix reported strong engagement across its Spanish-speaking markets without per-title figures. The 11-episode run closed out the de la Mora family arc with the operatic absurdity that had defined the show from the start. Manolo Caro had stated publicly that Season 3 was the intended ending, and the season functions as a genuine finale rather than a soft cancellation. No formal critic aggregate appeared on Rotten Tomatoes for Season 3, but audience scores tracked favourably on the platform's own metrics.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 earns its finale status - closing character arcs with the same mix of melodrama and wit that opened Season 1.
